comparator.name: Bachelor Medical Sciences and Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU/e's current official programme, Education Guide, learning-line, elective and final-project pages, checked 2026-10-05, identify Medical Sciences and Engineering as the medically oriented major within the three-year, 180-EC Biomedical Engineering bachelor. The official structure accounts for 105 EC of compulsory major and core study, a 15-EC Bachelor Final Project, a 15-EC USE/Impact of Technology learning line and 45 EC of free electives. The compulsory formation integrates anatomy, physiology, molecular and cell biology, chemistry, disease mechanisms and medical applications with mathematics, physics, programming, biomedical data, imaging, materials, laboratory research and challenge-based technology development. The complete 105/15/15/45 allocation is retained below rather than assigning unsupported individual credit values to topic and learning-line lists.
components: Compulsory Medical Sciences and Engineering programme

Compulsory formation across medical and life sciences, chemistry, mathematics, physics, programming and biomedical data, imaging, materials, laboratory research, medical technology and challenge-based projects.
A supervised research project completed in a TU/e research group.
Genuine programme choice within the elective part.
Genuine elective space preserved from the official curriculum structure.

alternatives.label: Molecular disease, human health and treatment
alternatives.concept: Builds a biomedical-science pathway from molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, anatomy and physiology into genetics, disease mechanisms, infection, pharmacology, laboratory investigation, epidemiology and quantitative evidence. It is the closest feasible UCR response to the medically oriented TU/e major, while not reproducing its physics, biomaterials, biomedical instrumentation, engineering-design or required final-project sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum sustains molecular and cellular mechanisms, human systems, disease, treatment, laboratory research and quantitative evidence across all three years.
progression: Life, health and biomedicine foundations precede molecular cell biology, laboratory work, anatomy, physiology, advanced disease, infection, pharmacology and genetics. Data, mathematics and empirical methods precede advanced quantitative and research work. Every prerequisite and planned 2026-2029 term offering was checked in the current enriched workbook.

alternatives.label: Biomedical data, imaging and diagnosis
alternatives.concept: Retains a substantial molecular, physiological and disease core while shifting the quantitative programme toward programming, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, machine learning, image processing, neural networks and robotics. It develops TU/e's explicit biomedical-data, imaging, diagnostic and technology-for-medical-research interests as a coherent second direction.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines biomedical mechanisms and disease with sustained programming, modelling, data analysis, imaging and intelligent-systems methods.
progression: Biomedical foundations, programming, data science and mathematical methods precede linear algebra, numerical methods, machine learning, probability, image processing, neural networks and robotics. Every prerequisite and planned 2026-2029 term offering was checked in the current enriched workbook.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, programming, linear algebra, numerical methods, image processing, neural networks and robotics replace epidemiology, infection and immunity, neurobiology, perception and action, medical and health psychology, and lifespan developmental psychology. The 45-EC shift follows the evidenced data, imaging and diagnostic-technology emphasis and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor.

blocks: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine directly addresses the programme's integrated medical and life-science foundation, but not its full engineering and technology scope.
Quantitative methods, biomedical data and technology
Research, public health and responsible innovation
Ethics provides normative analysis relevant to responsible medical technology, but does not reproduce TU/e's complete technology-specific USE/Impact of Technology formation.

TU/e requires a 15-EC biomedical Bachelor Final Project; no scheduled UCR course is treated as equivalent, and UCR's standardized optional independent-research opportunity is shown separately by the compiler.
TU/e preserves 45 EC of genuine free elective choice; it is not filled with match-optimising invented content.

candidates.label: Regenerative medicine, biomaterials and medical-technology design
candidates.reason: UCR has strong molecular and biomedical sciences and one life-science laboratory, but no biomaterials, tissue engineering, regenerative-medicine laboratory, biofabrication or medical-device-design sequence from which to build a separate 24-course programme without padding it with merely adjacent biology or data courses.

selection.assessment: The closest programme is a defensible 24-course response to the medically oriented major's molecular, cellular, physiological, disease, treatment, laboratory and evidence base. A second coherent curriculum follows the explicit biomedical-data, imaging and diagnosis cluster and passes all feasibility and pairwise-distinctness rules. A regenerative-medicine, biomaterials and medical-technology-design direction was also tested, but UCR lacks the materials, tissue-engineering, biofabrication and device-design sequence needed to sustain it as a third programme.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is explicitly the Medical Sciences and Engineering variant of TU/e's Biomedical Engineering bachelor. The reconstruction therefore follows that medically oriented major rather than the separate Biomedical Engineering major.

notes.text: TU/e Medical Sciences and Engineering integrates medical science with physics, chemistry, programming, biomedical data, imaging, biomaterials, laboratory work, challenge-based technology development and a required 15-EC Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers strong molecular and cellular biology, physiology, anatomy, disease, pharmacology, one life-science laboratory, mathematics, data science and imaging-related computation, but neither alternative reproduces TU/e's physics, biomaterials, tissue engineering, biomedical instrumentation, medical-device design, staged engineering laboratories or compulsory biomedical final project. TU/e also preserves 45 EC of genuine elective space.
